tasks.title: Generalize Slack transport and delivery for threads
tasks.spec: specs/channel-thread-routing/spec.md#Acknowledgement and result for thread-bound work are posted into the thread
tasks.description: Make the stateless mohist-slack protocol and Server delivery lineage capable of carrying Slack thread identity and sender facts end to end. Normalize thread_ts, the complete mention list, and human/Bot/unknown sender kind; carry thread provenance through connection launch, session metadata, terminal delivery, and the outbox; render outbound replies with thread_ts while preserving DM behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: SlackEnvelope and SlackIngressBody carry nullable threadTs, a de-duplicated full mention list, nullable senderSlackUserId, and normalized human/Bot/unknown sender kind; adapter tests cover a channel root event, a thread reply, multiple mentions, a Bot subtype, and an event with no stable user id.

Bot and unknown events retain their stable team/conversation/message identity, are acknowledged by the adapter, and cannot enter the Server inbox or become Agent input; no missing-user event is retried indefinitely.

Connection launch origin, coordinator fingerprint, session metadata labels, terminal delivery payload, outbox persistence/read model, and adapter Delivery carry optional thread identity; accepted channel work can be audited by workspace, channel, thread, and member.
The adapter calls Slack chat.postMessage with thread_ts for a threaded delivery and omits it for a DM delivery; terminal results and user-action acknowledgements retain their conversation target.
Existing DM routing and delivery behavior remains unchanged when threadTs is absent.
Relevant Server tests plus npm run typecheck -w packages/mohist-slack and npm run test:ci -w packages/mohist-slack pass without network access.
tasks.output: Thread-capable Slack adapter envelope/delivery contract and Server provenance/outbox plumbing with tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design D1 and D6 as one bounded transport/provenance module. Rename DmConversationId to ConversationId only in the shared connection-origin and delivery path; keep SlackDmSessionMappingStore DM-specific.

tasks.title: Deliver Owner-only channel launch and single-Agent thread continuity
tasks.spec: specs/channel-thread-routing/spec.md#A channel root mention launches work bound to the thread
tasks.description: Add durable per-Connection, per-workspace, per-channel thread bindings and extend the existing single ingress route with the safe Owner-only channel path. An unambiguous root mention launches through the existing Agent API and binds the session to the workspace channel thread; an unambiguous reply in a singly-bound thread reuses follow-up dispatch, with no new job or session.
acceptanceCriteria: A new SQLite-backed SlackThreadSessionMappingStore, row, DbContext registration, migration, and Connection-delete cleanup persist exactly one session per Connection plus workspace plus channel/conversation plus thread root timestamp. Its unique key and all lookups include workspace and channel, so equal root timestamps in two channels or two workspaces cannot share a binding.

The mapping store exposes both a per-Connection binding lookup and a workspace-plus-channel-plus-thread binding list/count query, allowing ingress to distinguish exactly one binding from multiple bindings without scanning inbox history or reading a different workspace's mappings.

An Owner root mention with a task creates exactly one AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, and AgentTurn through LaunchConnectionAsync, binds that session to the root thread, and acknowledges in the same thread; a bare mention creates no Agent resources and requests a task.

An Owner reply in a thread bound to exactly one Agent accepts a follow-up into that AgentSession without re-mention, preserves queued/executing acknowledgement semantics, and creates no new AgentJob or AgentSession. Any other Connection receiving that same unmentioned event ignores it without an inbox row, rejection, prompt, or Agent work.

The launch path persists its resolved session id on the accepted root inbox route before reply and idempotently binds that id. If a binding is missing, ingress repairs it from the matching workspace/channel root inbox route or the unique connection/channel/thread Session provenance before classifying the message.

The channel acceptance gate acknowledges and ignores normalized Bot or unknown senders, plain unbound-channel messages, and unbound-thread messages without writing an inbox row or persisting their text; a human non-Owner mention or bound-thread reply is explicitly rejected without Agent resources.

Duplicate root mentions and thread replies, including after adapter or Server restart, resolve to their original SessionInput and never create duplicate jobs, inputs, turns, or bindings. A fault-injection restart after LaunchConnectionAsync returns but before BindAsync persists still routes an unmentioned follow-up to the original session.

Server spec tests cover root launch, bare mention, follow-up after terminal and during execution, owner-only rejection, acknowledged ignored Bot/unknown input, an unmentioned single-Agent reply delivered to another Connection, provenance, equal root timestamps in distinct channels or workspaces, workspace-scoped binding-list cardinality, crash-window binding repair, and redelivery; npm test passes without real Slack, network, process, or wall-clock dependencies.
tasks.output: Usable Owner-only single-Agent channel and thread workflow backed by durable Server-held thread bindings.
tasks.notes: Implements design D2, D3, D7 and the single-target part of D4. Classify before inbox acceptance. Multi-target messages must fail closed with no Agent work; T-003 adds the once-only user prompt and full multi-Agent routing guardrails.

tasks.title: Add multi-Agent thread attribution and once-only ambiguity prompts
tasks.spec: specs/channel-attribution/spec.md#Mohist does not guess when the target Agent is ambiguous
tasks.description: Complete cross-Connection channel attribution for workspaces with several Mohist Bots. Resolve mentioned Bot identities within a workspace, preserve independent bindings for multiple Agents in one thread, and use a workspace-scoped first-writer-wins record so ambiguous input yields one choose-one prompt and no Agent work.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentConnectionStore exposes the active, identity-bound Bots for one workspace, and ingress resolves a message against that set rather than treating arbitrary human mentions as Bots.

A first explicit mention of a previously unbound Bot in an existing channel thread launches and binds a distinct AgentSession without changing or contaminating any existing Agent binding; an explicit single-Bot reply in a multi-Agent thread continues only that Bot's session.

A multi-Bot mention and an unmentioned reply whose workspace-plus-channel-plus-thread binding list contains multiple Agents start, continue, and persist no Agent work. Both produce at most one choose-one prompt: a root message is prompted at channel root and a thread reply is prompted in that same thread, including concurrent per-Connection ingress and Slack redelivery.

The workspace-scoped ambiguous-prompt dedup record is migration-backed, first-writer-wins on workspace plus conversation plus message identity, stores the optional inbound thread identity for delivery, and does not require adapter-held durable state.

Server spec tests cover multi-Bot mention suppression, one prompt across two Connection ingress calls, prompt redelivery suppression, multi-Agent thread no-mention suppression, explicit target isolation, the first second-Agent binding, and two workspaces sharing channel/thread identifiers without cross-workspace attribution or prompts; npm test passes using fake Slack/adapter interactions and injectable time only.
Update docs/agent-connections.md and design/slack-agent-connection.md implementation-gap sections to state that channel/thread routing and multi-Agent attribution are implemented.
tasks.output: Complete multi-Agent channel/thread attribution with durable once-only ambiguity feedback and regression coverage.
tasks.notes: Implements design D4 and D5 and completes the multi-Agent requirements in both specs. The ambiguity prompt uses the race-winning Connection's existing outbox; no workspace-wide sender or cross-Server coordination is introduced.
